concept.name: Private key
concept.definition: A private key is a secret 256-bit number that controls an externally owned blockchain account: whoever knows it can sign transactions and spend the account's funds, so it must never be revealed.
concept.intuition: The private key is the one true password to your coins — there is no recovery desk if it leaks or is lost.
concept.mechanics: Wallets generate a random private key (64 hex characters); the corresponding public key is derived via elliptic-curve multiplication (ECDSA/secp256k1 on Ethereum), and the address is the last 20 bytes of the Keccak-256 hash of the public key. Signing a transaction with the private key proves authorization without revealing the key.
concept.formula: public_key = private_key × G (elliptic curve point multiplication with generator G); address = last 20 bytes of Keccak256(public_key).
concept.failure_modes: Key theft (malware, phishing, insecure backups) gives irreversible control of funds; key loss is final because no one can regenerate a private key from an address — the derivation is one-way.
concept.misconceptions: A private key cannot be recovered from the public address — reversing the hash or the elliptic-curve multiplication is computationally infeasible. Changing a wallet password does not change or protect an already-leaked key.
concept.example: A private key looks like ffffffff...415f (64 hex chars); exposing it once in a screenshot or cloud note lets anyone sweep the account's entire balance in a single signed transaction.
